READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

A. Nehemiah's summary of YHWH's gracious acts and covenant faithfulness (cf. Neh. 9:17) may have come from Ezra's reading of the Book of Moses (i.e., Pentateuch).

 

B. The chapter outlines as

1. YHWH as creator (Gen. 1-11), Neh. 9:6

2. YHWH's choice of Abraham (Gen. 12-50), Neh. 9:7-8

3. YHWH's actions in the Exodus (Exodus), Neh. 9:9-14

4. YHWH's faithful care and provision during the wilderness wandering period (Numbers), Neh. 9:15-21

5. YHWH's promises to Abraham fulfilled (period of the conquest, i.e., Joshua), Neh. 9:22-25

6. Israel's further rebellion (period of the Judges), Neh. 9:26-31

7. YHWH's covenant faithfulness and Israel's unfaithfulness continue (the period of the Monarchy), Neh. 9:32-38

 

C. Nehemiah 9 shows the theological basis of Israel's history — YHWH's faithfulness to His covenant; Israel's unfaithfulness to His covenant. It was not YHWH's powerlessness, but Israel's sin that brought destruction and exile; however, it is because of YHWH's character and power that Israel  exists and is back in the Promised Land!

 

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:2 "descendants of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:2 "descendants of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners" This VERB (BDB 95, KB 110, Niphal IMPERFECT) means "to withdraw from," "separate ourselves from." This withdrawal was for the stated purpose of obeying YHWH's commands (cf. Exod. 33:16; Lev. 20:24,26; Ezra 6:21; 9:1; 10:1). To worship and obey YHWH meant a complete break with the pagan and semi-pagan culture and practices (cf. Lev. 20:24,26; e.g., marriages to foreign women).

▣ "confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers" This VERB (BDB 392, KB 389 II, Hithpael IMPERFECT) means "to confess" (cf. Lev. 5:5; 16:21; Ezra 10:1; Neh. 1:6; Dan. 9:4,20). Apparently this confession involved personal and national sin (e.g., Lev. 26-40; Jer. 3:25; 14:20).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:3 "they stood in their place"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:3 "they stood in their place" This seems to refer to Neh. 8:4 (cf. Neh. 9:4).

▣ "they read from the book of the law of the Lord their God for a fourth of the day" These returnees longed to be instructed from the Law of Moses. It seems at this point that a major turning point in the life of the Jews occurred. Instead of being primarily people of the temple (ritual, liturgy, and form) they became people of the Book (the influence of the synagogue). This was a reading/teaching session lasting three hours in the morning (Bible study) and three hours in the afternoon (confession and worship).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:4 If Neh. 9:3 refers to Neh. 8:4, then this verse must refer to a separate platform. The names mentioned here refer to the Levites of Neh. 8:7, who translated and interpreted Ezra's (and the men standing with him) words.

These two groups may have been involved in antiphonal reading interspersed with translation and interpretation.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:5 The Septuagint adds the phrase "and Ezra said. . ." Apparently it is asserting the authorship of chapter 9 to Ezra instead of the Levite leaders, as the MT implies. The rest of this chapter is a history of God's faithful covenant promises and the people's unfaithful responses.

▣ "Arise, bless" These are both IMPERATIVES. The first VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE) means "to stand up." Apparently unlike Ezra's first reading of the Law (cf. chapter 8), the people did not stand up the entire time (cf. Neh. 8:5).

The second VERB (BDB 138, KB 159 II, used twice, the first a Piel IMPERATIVE, the second a Piel IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) means to praise or adore for having special power (cf. Neh. 8:6; 1 Chr. 29:20).

▣ "the Lord your God" The covenant name of God, YHWH, translated Lord, is from the Hebrew VERB "to be" and refers to the ever-living, only-living One!

Special Topic: Names for Deity, C. and D.

▣ "forever and ever" This is literally "from everlasting to everlasting." It is used of YHWH in Ps. 41:13; 106:48.

Special Topic: Forever ('olam)

▣ "Your glorious name" The name is a Hebraic idiom for a person (e.g., Exod. 32:33; 1 Chr. 28:13; Ps. 72:19; Acts 1:18; 4:10). God is glorious.

Special Topic: Glory (kabod, OT)

Special Topic: "The Name" of YHWH

▣ "above all blessing and praise" The TEV catches the meaning as "although no human praise is great enough."

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:6 This verse is an emphasis on God as the only (in the spirit of Exod. 20:2-3 and Deut. 6:4) Creator and Sustainer of the Universe. Here creation is attributed to YHWH. Usually it is attributed to Elohim (cf. Genesis 1).

Special Topic: Monotheism

▣ "You have made the heavens" This phrase is parallel to "the earth and all that is on it." "Heavens" here refers to the atmosphere of this planet (cf. Gen. 1:1).

Special Topic: Heaven

▣ "the heaven of heavens with all their hosts" This seems to refer to the ancient association of heavenly bodies (e.g., sun, moon, planets, stars, comets) with gods or angels (cf. Neh. 9:6g; Deut. 4:19; Job 38:7).

There has been an ongoing discussion among the rabbis as to how many "heavens" there are and to what they refer. The "highest" heaven would be God's throne. Some see this as the third heaven (cf. 2 Cor. 12:2), while others assert "seventh heaven" (b. Hagigah 11b).

In this context the "heavens of heavens" refers to the starry heavens (cf. Deut. 10:14; Ps. 148:3-4) that personified worship and praise to God.

Special Topic: The Heavens and the Third Heaven

NASB, REB   "You give life to all of them"
NKJV, Peshitta   "You preserve them all"
NRSV   "to all of them you give life"
TEV   "you gave life to all"
NJB, JPSOA   "You keep them all alive"
LXX   "You give everything life"

This VERB (BDB 310, KB 309, Piel PARTICIPLE) can mean

  1. preserve alive (NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta, cf. Exod. 1:17,18,22; Deut. 6:24; 20:16)
  2. give life (NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, NIV, REB, LXX, cf. Job 33:4)
  3. restore life (cf. Deut. 32:39; 1 Sam. 2:6; Hos. 6:2)

YHWH is creator, sustainer, and restorer of life (cf. Col. 1:16-17)!

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:7 "the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7 "the Lord God" This is YHWH Elohim. This combined title occurs first in Gen. 2:4.

Special Topic: Names for Deity, C. and D.

▣ "Who chose Abraham" This VERB (BDB 103, KB 119, Qal PERFECT) refers to God's choice. Here of Abraham (cf. Genesis 12); in Deut. 7:6-7 of Israel as a people. This refers theologically to the initiation of a covenant relationship. God must initiate. The burning question is does He call, choose, initiate to all or to some select group? Even in the OT, the choice of Abraham was a means to choose all humans (cf. Gen. 12:3); the choice of Israel was a choice for all humans (cf. Exod. 19:4-6, esp. Neh. 9:5c).

Special Topic: He Chose Us

Special Topic: Election/Predestination and the Need for a Theological Balance

Special Topic: Predestination (Calvinism) vs. Human Free Will (Arminianism)

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

▣ "brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees" Originally Abraham's family were apparently worshipers of the moon god (cf. Gen. 11:31). Ur was one of several centers for moon god (i.e., Sin or Zin) worship. At this point, in history all were polytheists (many gods) or henotheists (many gods, but one special god for me).

Special Topic: Chaldeans

Special Topic: Moon Worship

▣ "gave him the name Abraham" His original name "Abram" means "exalted Father" (BDB 4, KB 10). The name Abraham means "chief of a multitude" (BDB 4, KB, cf. Gen. 17:5, where it is defined as "the father of a multitude of nations").

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:7-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7-8 This seems to deal with God's choosing and covenanting with Abraham (cf. Genesis 12-18).

Special Topic: Covenant Promises to the Patriarchs

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:8 "You found his heart faithful before You"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:8 "You found his heart faithful before You" Because of the use of the word "faithful," this must refer to Gen. 15:6 (cf. Rom. 4:3,9,22; Gal. 3:6; James 2:23), which refers to God's promise of descendants. Abraham's faith is fully revealed in Gen. 22 (cf. James 2:22).

Special Topic: Believe, Trust, Faith, and Faithfulness in the OT

Special Topic: The Heart

▣ "And made a covenant with him" This covenant is first delineated in Gen. 12:1-3, but reaffirmed in chapters 15 and 17.

Special Topic: Covenant

▣ "give him the land of the Canaanite" This aspect of the covenant is fully delineated in Gen. 15:17-21. For a full discussion of these tribes of Canaan see Ezra 9:1.

Special Topic: Pre-Israelite Inhabitants of Palestine

▣ "to his descendants" This is literally the term "seed." In the OT it focuses on the Jewish people, but in the NT Paul sees it as referring uniquely to Christ (cf. Gal. 3:15-22).

▣ "You have fulfilled Your promise" This relates to Gen. 15:12-21, which refers to the Exodus from Egypt and the conquest of Canaan.

▣ "For You are righteous" This relates to YHWH's character (cf. 2 Chr. 12:6; Ezra 9:15), but the same term is used in Neh. 9:33, translated "just" and refers to His actions (i.e., judgments, cf. Exod. 9:27; Ps. 119:137; 145:17). The specific text that relates to the reason for the Canaanite defeat is Deut. 9:4-6.

Special Topic: Righteousness

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:9-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:9-14 This deals with the period of the Exodus and wilderness wandering period. God's promise and fulfillment of bringing the children of Israel out of Egypt is a recurrent theme (e.g., Ps. 78:12ff; 105:23ff; 106:7ff; 135:8ff; 136:10ff).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:9 "You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:9 "You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt" This relates to Exod. 2:25; 3:7 (Acts 7:34).

▣ "And heard their cry by the Red Sea" This refers specifically to Exodus 14.

Special Topic: The Red Sea

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:10 This verse refers to the series of plagues that YHWH sent through Moses (cf. Exodus 7-11). These plagues target and repudiate the nature and animal gods of Egypt. YHWH wants Egyptians to believe in Him also (cf. Neh. 9:10d; Exod. 9:14-16).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:11 "their pursuers You hurled into the depths"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:11 "their pursuers You hurled into the depths" This refers to Exod. 14, especially Neh. 9:26-31.

▣ "Like a stone into raging waters" This is almost an exact quote from the Song of Moses in Exod. 15:5,10.

Special Topic: Waters

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:12 "a pillar of fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:12 "a pillar of fire" This refers to Shekinah cloud of glory (physical symbol of the presence of YHWH) that separated the children of Israel from the army of Pharaoh, and led them throughout the wilderness wandering period (e.g., Exod. 13:22; 14:19-24; 16:10; 19:9,16; 24:15-18; 34:5; 40:34-38). This is referred to again in Neh. 9:19. 

▣ "the way" See Special Topic: The Route of the Exodus.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:13 "Then You came down on Mount Sinai"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:13 "Then You came down on Mount Sinai" See Special Topic: Location of Mt. Sinai.

▣ "You gave them just ordinances and true laws" There are some cultural examples similar to the decalog.

  1. The Laws of Lipit-Ishtar (Sumerian), from the king of Isin (1934-1924 B.C.)
  2. The Laws of Eshnunna (old Babylonian), dating about 1800 B.C. from the reign of Dadusha, king of Ashnunna
  3. The Code of Hammurabi (old Babylon) from the king of Babylon, Hammurabi (1728-1686 B.C.)
  4. The law codes of the Hittite kings Mupsilis I or Hattusilis I, from about 1650 B.C.
  5. The Mesopotamian law codes focus primarily on civil laws, while the biblical laws focus primarily on religious/cultic laws. ". . .we might suggest a civil bias in all cuneiform law and a cultic bias in Israelite law. . ., in Mesopotamia, offense is ultimately viewed in relation to society; while in Israel, all offense is ultimately against God." Walton, p. 80.
  6. Albrecht Alt in Essays on Old Testament History and Religion, Oxford, 1966, pp. 81-132, has identified two types of laws:
    1. casuistic, which use conditional clauses. It is characterized by an "if. . .then" structure. It does not appeal to religious or societal norms but states a prohibition and consequence.
    2. apodictic, which does not use conditional clauses
      (1) Exodus 21 and Deut. 27:15-26 use the third person and relate to individual, specific cases
      (2) Lev. 18:7-17 and Exodus 20/Deuteronomy 5 use the second person and are more general in scope.
    3. Mesopotamian law is primarily casuistic while Israelite law is primarily apodictic.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:14 This verse, like Neh. 9:13, relates to the giving of the Ten Commandments to Moses on Mt. Sinai recorded in Exodus 19-20; see note online.

The phrase "Your holy sabbath" probably refers to Exod. 20:8-11, which is a theological development of the seventh day of rest of Gen. 2:1-3.

Special Topic: Sabbath (OT)

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB   "Through Your servant Moses"
NKJV   "By the hand of Moses Your servant"

The NKJV retains the literal idiom. Moses is said to have "written" God's laws several times (cf. Exod. 17:14; 24:4,7; 34:27,28; Num. 33:2; Deut. 31:9,22,24-26)!

Special Topic: Covenant

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:15 "You provided bread from heaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:15 "You provided bread from heaven" This daily provision of manna is described in Exodus 16, especially vv. 14-15,31.

Special Topic: Manna

▣ "You brought forth water from a rock" This must have occurred regularly, but only two times are recorded (Exod. 17:6; Num. 20:7-13).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:15-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:15-21 This is a description of the wilderness wandering period and God's unique care amidst the children of Israel's rebellion (Ezra's theme in chapter 9).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:16-17 Here is the recurrent theme of the chapter.

  1. God's faithfulness and love, Neh. 9:17b
  2. Israel's unfaithfulness and rebellion, Neh. 9:16-17a

YHWH's righteousness and Israel's rebellion are graphically revealed in Deut. 9:4-6,7,13,24,27.

9:16
NASB   "they became stubborn"
NKJV   "hardened their necks"
NRSV, JPSOA, LXX   "stiffened their necks"
TEV   "grew. . .stubborn"
NJB   "grew obstinate"
Peshitta   "they were stubborn"

The VERB (BDB 904 I, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERFECT) and the NOUN (BDB 791) both denote purposeful rejection of truth (i.e., rebellion, cf. Neh. 9:17,29; 2 Chr. 30:8; 36:13; Jer. 7:26; 17:23; 19:15).

Special Topic: Stubbornness (OT)

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:17 "Your wondrous deeds"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:17 "Your wondrous deeds" This VERB (BDB 810, KB 927, Niphal PARTICIPLE), can mean "difficult" (cf. Deut. 17:8; Pro. 30:18) or "wonderful" (cf. Exod. 3:20; Ps. 78:12-16). In this passage, like so many Psalms, it refers to God's mighty, powerful, extraordinary acts of deliverance during the exodus, wanderings, and conquest.

Special Topic: Wonderful Things

▣ "appointed a leader to return to their slavery" This relates specifically to Num. 14:4. The precursor is found in Exod. 14:10-12 and Num. 11:1-9.

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, LXX, NET   "in Egypt"
NKJV     -------
JPSOA   "to their slavery"
Peshitta   "to their evil works"

The MT has "to their bondage (BDB 715) in rebellion" (BDB 598). The terms "in rebellion" and "in Egypt" are very similar.

  1. in rebellion ‒ במרים
  2. in Egypt ‒ במצרימ

The UBS Text Project, p. 538, gives option #2 a "C" rating (i.e., considerable doubt). So the question is, "Does this phrase refer to an attitude or a location?" Egyptian "affliction" is mentioned in v. 9 and again "Egypt" in v. 18.

▣ "You are a God" There are six specific things stated about God's character.

  1. forgiving (BDB 699, used exclusively of God's forgiveness)
  2. gracious (BDB 337, cf. Deut. 4:31; 2 Chr. 30:9)
  3. compassionate (BDB 933)
  4. slow to anger (cf. Num.14:18)
  5. abounding in lovingkindness (BDB 338, Covenant loyalty, see Special Topic: Lovingkindness (hesed)
  6. He did not forsake them!

This is one of a select number of OT texts that delineate the basic nature of God — Exod. 34:6-7; Ps. 103:8; and Joel 2:13.

Part of this text's litany of God's characteristics became a standard way of referring to His character (cf. Ps. 86:15; 145:8; Jonah 4:2). This is who God is! Rejoice and be glad!

Believers' hope is based on the unchanging character of God. Remember the list is given in a verse that describes Israel's intentional rejection of God and His word.

Special Topic: Characteristics of Israel's God

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:18 "they made for themselves a calf of molten metal"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:18 "they made for themselves a calf of molten metal" The calf may have been a physical representation of YHWH, not another god (cf. Exodus 32).

▣ "and committed great blasphemies" There is a series of sins recorded in Exodus 32.

  1. idolatry (cf. LXX & Vulgate) or at least making a physical image of YHWH (cf. Exod. 20:4-5)
  2. drunkenness
  3. sexual promiscuity (cf. Exod. 32:6, "rose up to play" means a sexual orgy, cf. Gen. 26:18 for another use of this phrase)

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:19 "the pillar of cloud"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:19 "the pillar of cloud" See Special Topic: Coming On the Clouds

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:20 "You gave Your good Spirit to instruct them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:20 "You gave Your good Spirit to instruct them" God's "good spirit" does not necessarily refer to the NT Trinitarian understanding of the Holy Spirit, the third person of the Trinity. In the OT God's Spirit is a way of referring to His will being accomplished (cf. Gen. 1:2). In this context it is probably parallel to God's angel who accompanied Israel during the wilderness wandering period (cf. Exod. 3:2; 14:19; 23:20,23,34; 33:2).

Also, God's Spirit is a way of referring to revelation or inspiration (cf. Neh. 9:30; Ps. 143:10). He (NT Trinitarian sense) is the agent of inspiration (cf. Neh. 9:30; Num. 11:17,25,29; 1 Sam. 10:6,9-11; 2 Sam. 23:2; 1 Kgs. 22:24; 1 Chr. 12:18; 2 Chr. 24:20; Isa. 11:2; 42:1; Ezek. 11:5,24; Hos. 9:7; Joel 2:28-29; Micah 3:8; Zech. 7:12).

Special Topic: Spirit in the Bible

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:21 Even though the wilderness wandering period was a time of judgment because of their unbelief, God was with them in a personal, powerful, daily way. The rabbis later called this time "the honeymoon" period because of YHWH's tender care and provision.

The term "forty" is a round, symbolic number. This period only lasted 38 years. The specific reference to the clothes not wearing out is from Deut. 8:4; 29:5.

Special Topic: Symbolic Numbers in Scripture, #7

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:22 This refers to Joshua's conquest on the eastern side of the Jordan (cf. Num. 21:21-35; Ps. 135:11; 136:19-20).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:23 "You made their sons numerous as the stars of heaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:23 "You made their sons numerous as the stars of heaven" This was part of the Abrahamic covenant (cf. Gen. 15:5; 22:17; 26:4; Exod. 32:13, i.e., numerous descendants also referred to as "like the sand of the sea," cf. Gen. 22:12; 32:12; Isa. 48:19; Hos. 1:10). For similar hyperbole see Gen. 13:16; 16:10; 17:20; 28:14.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:23-25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:23-25 This seems to refer to Joshua's conquest of the land of Canaan.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:26 "And cast Your law behind their backs"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:26 "And cast Your law behind their backs" This is a Hebrew idiom for being out of sight, being out of mind (cf. Isa. 38:17). It has the connotation of willful rejection (cf. 1 Kgs. 14:9; Ezek. 23:35 and the same concept is in Ps. 50:17).

▣ "And killed Your prophets" God's people did not want to hear from God through His spokespersons so they silenced the speaker!

Special Topic: Prophecy (OT)

▣ "return" See Special Topic: Repentance in the OT.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:26-31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:26-31 This refers to the period of the Judges, which was one of the darkest periods of Israel's history. Cycle after cycle of sin and restoration!

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:27 The recurrent theme of YHWH's patience, love, and covenant loyalty is contrasted with Israel's rebellion, generation after generation (cf. Neh. 9:28).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:29 "to turn them back"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:29 "to turn them back" See Special Topic: Repentance in the OT.

NASB   "they acted arrogantly"
NKJV   "they acted proudly"
NRSV, JPSOA   "they acted presumptuously"
TEV   "in pride they rejected"
NJB   "they became arrogant"

This VERB (BDB 267, KB 268, Hiphil PERFECT) implies the willful rejection of God's authority expressed through His prophets (cf. Neh. 9:30) and His word. Often one's personal, cultural, or national opinions are substituted for God's truth (e.g., false prophets).

The LXX characterizes Israel's repeated unfaithful actions and attitudes.

  1. "did not listen"
  2. "sinned against your commandments and judgments"
  3. "presented a disobedient back"
  4. "stiffened their neck"
  5. "did not listen"

▣ "By which if a man observes them he shall live" This is the OT understanding of salvation (cf. Lev. 18:5; Gal. 3:12). However, the repeated failure of each and every generation of the sons of Adam forced YHWH to bring about a "new covenant" (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-38) based on God's performance (in Christ) only dependent on a faithful human reception. The goal is still the same—a righteous people, but the mechanism has changed; an internal law/a new heart/a new spirit!

Special Topic: Keep

▣ "And they turned a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck" This terminology refers to Deut. 9:6, 7,13,24,27.

Special Topic: Stubbornness (OT)

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:30 "the peoples of the lands"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:30 "the peoples of the lands" In Ezra (Ezra 3:3; 9:1,2,11; 10:2,11) and Nehemiah (Neh. 9:30; 10:29,31,32) this means native inhabitants (i.e., those who survived the deportations and those resettled in Palestine and the resulting intermarriages). Earlier in the OT it referred to either (1) the wealthy land owners or (2) the people who had legal rights as citizens.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:31 God's covenant judgment (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28) was always an attempt to cause Israel to repent and return. However, grace and mercy rejected results in judgment even beyond this life. God chose Israel to choose the world! He retained a faithful remnant to accomplish His Messianic promises and world evangelization!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:32 "our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and lovingkindness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:32 "our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and lovingkindness" Again the character and faithfulness of YHWH, in contrast to His people, is emphasized (cf. Neh. 9:33). This is the recurrent theme.

The term "great" (BDB 152) is attributed

  1. several times (cf. Neh. 1:5; Deut. 7:21; 10:17; Ps. 77:13; 95:3; Jer. 32:18; Dan. 9:4)
  2. to Elohim (cf. Neh. 8:6; 2 Chr. 2:5)
  3. to YHWH (cf. Exod. 18:11; 1 Chr. 16:25; Ps. 48:1; 96:4; 99:2; 135:5; 145:3; Jer. 10:6)

God's power is great (Num. 14:17); God's name is great (2 Sam. 7:26; 1 Chr. 17:24); God's works are great (Ps. 92:5).

The term "awesome" (BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE) is used in several but related senses in connection to God.

  1. God's redemptive acts (e.g., Deut. 10:21)
  2. description of God Himself (e.g., Deut. 7:21; 10:17; Neh. 1:5; 4:18; 9:32)
    1. of His name (e.g., Deut. 28:58)
    2. of His appearance (e.g., Jdg. 13:6; Isa. 64:3)

Humans tremble or should tremble at the presence or even mention of the God of creation.

The last two in the list are synonymous. God's power is established by His faithfulness to His promises. These last two characteristics often appear together (cf. Neh. 1:5; 9:32; Deut. 7:2,9,12; 1 Kgs. 8:23; 2 Chr. 6:14; Dan. 9:4).

A good article on the relationship between berith (covenant) and hesed (lovingkindness) is Edmund Jacob, Theology of the Old Testament, pp. 103-107.

Special Topic: Lovingkindness (hesed)

▣ "From the days of the kings of Assyria to this day" Assyria took the Northern Ten Tribes captive in 722 B.C. For a list of their kings in sequence see Special Topic: Kings of Assyria

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:32-37
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:32-37 These verses deal with the period of the United (Saul, David, and Solomon) and Divided Monarchy (Israel until 922 B.C. and Judah until 586 B.C.).

Special Topic: Kings of the Divided Kingdom

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:33 "You are just in all that has come upon us"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:33 "You are just in all that has come upon us" The consequences for covenant violation are clearly spelled out in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. God's judgments are both judicially fair and redemptively purposeful.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:35 "the broad and rich land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:35 "the broad and rich land" The Promised Land could hardly be characterized as "spacious," so it must be used metaphorically for a place of freedom (cf. Exod. 3:8).

Canaan was a very fertile land in Moses' day (cf. Exod. 3:8,17; 13:5; Num. 13:23,27).

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:36 "Behold, we are slaves today"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:36 "Behold, we are slaves today" This refers to the continuing domination, albeit benevolent, under Persia.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:38-10:27 "leaders. . .Levites. . .priests"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:38-10:27 "leaders. . .Levites. . .priests" The leaders are mentioned in Neh. 10:1,14-27; the Levites in Neh. 10:9-13; and priests in Neh. 10:2-8 (cf. Neh. 12:1-7). There has been much discussion among scholars whether individuals or families are listed. It is also unusual that Ezra is not mentioned, however, he was a member of the first named priestly family (Seraiah).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought provoking, not definitive.

1. How are Neh. 9:1-2 related to the Day of Atonement?

2. Is confession individual or corporate or both? How does this affect the way we pray/confess today?

3. Who verbalizes the Psalm (Neh. 9:5-32)?

4. How is the group on the platform in Neh. 9:4 related to the group speaking in Neh. 9:5?

5. Outline the different periods of Israel's history alluded to in the Psalm.

6. Why is Neh. 9:17 so important?

7.  Explain the OT concept of "Spirit." How do Neh. 9:20 and Neh. 9:30 relate?

8. Explain the significance of Neh. 9:31.

entries.title: Nehemiah 9:38 "We are making an agreement in writing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:38 "We are making an agreement in writing" Although the word "covenant" is not used here, a similar but rare word is employed. The term "agreement" is really from the Hebrew root "amen" and should be translated "firm agreement" (BDB 53). The VERB "making" is the Hebrew term "to cut" (BDB 503, KB 500, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE). This is often associated with the common phrase "to cut a covenant."

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:28 This mentions several groups that served in the temple.

▣ "all those who had knowledge and understanding" See note at Neh. 8:2. This seems to refer to the children.

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:29 "a curse and an oath to walk in God's law"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:29 "a curse and an oath to walk in God's law" This is a covenant renewal service much like Jos. 8:30-35 and 24:1ff. These renewal ceremonies were based on the covenant blessings and cursings summarized in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. Obedience and disobedience had consequences in this life and the next!

The term "walk" is a biblical metaphor for lifestyle faith. God's word/teachings are a path for His people to follow (e.g., Ps. 119:105; Pro. 6:23).

▣ "the commandments. . .ordinances. . .statutes" The revelation of God to God is characterized by several terms. Notice the list and parallelism of Ps. 19:7-9.

Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation

NASB   "God our Lord"
NKJV, NRSV, TEV   "the Lord our Lord"
NJB   "Yahweh our Lord"

The first term is YHWH, the covenant name for God (cf. Gen. 2:4). The second is Adon, which meant husband, owner, master, or lord.

Special Topic: Names for Deity, C.

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:30 "and that we will not give our daughters to the people of the land or take their daughters for our sons"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:30 "and that we will not give our daughters to the people of the land or take their daughters for our sons" This does not refer to racial exclusion, but religious exclusion (cf. Exod. 34:12-16; Ezra 9:10; Neh. 13:23-28). This was a major issue in restored Judah.

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:31 "As for the peoples of the land who bring wares or any grain on the sabbath day to sell"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:31 "As for the peoples of the land who bring wares or any grain on the sabbath day to sell" The indigenous habitants of the Persian province who were supposedly "YHWHistic" were violating the Sabbath requirements. This is one example of the problems of trying to work with or associate with the inhabitants who were in the land when the returnees arrived.

Special Topic: Sabbath (OT)

▣ "and we will forgo the crops the seventh year" This is a second feature of Mosaic law which was a means of acknowledging YHWH's ownership of the land and His care and concern for the needy (cf. Exod. 23:10-11; Lev. 25:4-7,20-22).

▣ "and the exaction of every debt" This is a third element related to Moses' law. All debts were cancelled on the seventh year (cf. Deut. 15:1-2; 31:10), which was called the Sabbath year. They were serious about reinstating the Mosaic law in its fullness. YHWH had a special care and concern for the poor and powerless.

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:32 "to contribute yearly one third of a shekel for the service of the house of our God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:32 "to contribute yearly one third of a shekel for the service of the house of our God" In Exod. 30:11-16, it is a half of a shekel given to the tabernacle, but it is not given annually. Exactly what the fee paid for is delineated in Neh. 10:33. In the pre-exilic period, the king supported the cost of the temple, but in the post-exilic community the cost was shared among the people.

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:33 "the showbread"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:33 "the showbread" See Exod. 25:23-30.

Special Topic: Show Bread of the Presence

▣ "the continual grain offering" See Num. 28:1-8.

▣ "the continual burnt offering" See Exod. 29:38-42; Num. 28:1-.8

▣ "the sabbaths, the new moon, for the appointed times" See Num. 28:9-10,11-15; 29:39-40.

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel

▣ "for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel" See Lev. 4:1-5:13 and Num. 15:23-29.

Special Topic: Atonement

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:34 "we cast lots for the supply of wood"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:34 "we cast lots for the supply of wood" The casting of lots was a mechanical way (like the Urim and Thummim) to discern God's will. In this case the lots help divide the responsibility for wood for the burnt offerings among the returnees. Each family was responsible for a period of time. This later turns into a feast (cf. Josephus, Wars 17.6)

Special Topic: Urim and Thummim

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:35 "the first fruits"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:35 "the first fruits" Giving God the first ripened fruit was a way to show God's ownership of the entire harvest. These offerings helped support the priests. See Exod. 22:29; 23:19; 34:26; Deut. 26:1-11; and Ezek. 44:30.

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:36 "the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:36 "the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle" this was a way to show God's ownership of all things. See Exodus 13.

Special Topic: Firstborn

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:37 "we will also bring the first of our dough"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:37 "we will also bring the first of our dough" See Lev. 23:17.

▣ "and the tithe of our ground to the Levites" See Lev. 27:30.

Special Topic: Thithing in the Mosaic Legislation

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:38 "The priest. . .shall be with the Levites"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:38 "The priest. . .shall be with the Levites" This was one of the checks and balances procedures installed to insure the taxation system.

▣ "the tenth of the tithes" The Levites were required to tithe to the priests (cf. Num. 18:26). In the OT there were many Levites so the priests got all they needed from their tithe, but in these days there were few Levites. The priests, however, did not want to alter the Mosaic regulations.

There is some confusion about exactly how the tithing system in Israel worked. From Deut. 14:22-29

  1. individuals brought a tithe to the central sanctuary for two years
  2. the third year the tithe was paid locally to benefit the poor
  3. every seventh year the fields lay fallow so there was no tithe of produce

In this passage (Neh. 10:32-39), all non-produce items were brought to the priests in Jerusalem, but the produce was brought to the Levites in the local towns, who then tithed that to Jerusalem. The special offerings like "the first fruits" or "first born" were also taken to Jerusalem.

Special Topic: Tithing in the Mosaic Legislation

entries.title: Nehemiah 10:39 "new wine"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:39 "new wine" See Special Topic: Biblical Attitudes Toward Alcohol and Alcoholism.

▣ "Thus we will not neglect the house of our God" All of the provisions mentioned in Neh. 10:34-39 were to equip the temple and its personnel for its regular duties.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:1 "the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:1 "the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem" Since the terrible siege of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar in 586 B.C., no one wanted to live in the city. The leaders (the wealthy laymen, cf. Neh. 11:3) and the temple personnel were the only large groups that lived within the city's walls (cf. Neh. 11:3; 2:16-17). They were to be joined by 10% of the Jewish population of the surrounding towns plus any volunteers (cf. Neh. 11:2). This involved leaving established homes and farms. This same subject is first introduced in Neh. 7:4.

▣ "cast lots" This VERB (BDB 656, KB 709, Hiphil PERFECT) means "casting lots (cf. 1 Chr. 24:31; 25:8; 26:13-14; Esth. 3:7; 9:24). This had religious connotations (cf. Neh. 10:34; Num. 26:55-56; Jos. 14:2; Pro. 16:33; 18:18). It was a way to know the will of YHWH, as was the Urim and Thummim (cf. Exod. 28:30; Lev. 8:8; Num. 27:21). The Urim was used exclusively by the High Priest, but "lots" were used to know YHWH's will by others (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 840-842).

Special Topic: Urim and Thummim

▣ "the holy city" This was a way of referring to the place where YHWH dwelt (cf. Isa. 48:2; 52:1; Dan. 9:24).

Special Topic: Holy

Special Topic: Jerusalem

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:3 "Now these are the heads of the provinces who lived in Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:3 "Now these are the heads of the provinces who lived in Jerusalem" This list is quite similar to 1 Chronicles 9; about half of the names are the same. The exact relationship between these two lists as with other lists in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, is uncertain.

▣ "each lived on his own property" The term "property" (BDB 28) usually meant "to grasp" or "to seize," but in connection to tribal allotments it has the connotation of given by YHWH (both as a promise to Abraham, cf. Gen. 5:12-21 and by the Urim in Joshua 13-19).

▣ "Israelites" This refers to Jewish laymen. This verse lists the different elements of Jewish society. The different kinds of temple personnel and lay persons are included.

▣ "temple servants" This term (BDB 682) in post-exilic texts always has the ARTICLE and is PLURAL. It designates a temple labor force. The origin of the term may be "the given ones," referring to those non-Israelites defeated in battle by King David and given to the temple to help the Levites (cf. Ezra 8:20); therefore, they are like "Solomon's servants" (cf. Ezra 2:58; Neh. 7:60; 11:3).

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:4 "sons of Judah. . .sons of Benjamin"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:4 "sons of Judah. . .sons of Benjamin" The preponderance of returning Jews were from these two tribes because they made up the last tribal groups to be exiled. Simeon was also part of the tribe of Judah but had lost their tribal identity.

▣ "Perez" See Gen. 38:29.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:5 "the son of the Shilonite"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:5 "the son of the Shilonite" This designation is surprising in a list of names (cf. 1 Chr. 9:5). There is no first name associated with this place (Shiloh, a city in Ephraim). It is possible that the consonants of "Shilonites" should refer to "Shelah," one of Judah's sons in Gen. 38:5,26, therefore, "Shelanite" (cf. Derek Kidner, Tyndale Commentary, p. 118), which is the way NEB and REB translate 1 Chr. 9:5 and the form appears in Num. 26:20.

11:8
NASB, NKJV, JPSOA   "after him"
NRSV, NJB   "his brothers"
TEV   "close relatives"
NET, NIV   "his followers"
NEB, REB   "his kinsmen"

This Hebrew term (BDB 29) has a large usage. All of the above translations are a possibility. For me those that focus on kinship fit the context best. However, "brothers" involves a textual emendation.

The UBS Text Project, p. 539, gives a "B" rating (some doubt) to "and after him" (MT).

  1. and after him ‒ ואחריו
  2. and his brothers ‒ ואחיו (LXX)

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:9 "their overseer"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:9 "their overseer" This term (BDB 824) means "commissioner, deputy, overseer. It is used in Neh. 11:22 for a leader of Levites. It is used of the king's officers in 2 Chr. 24:11 and of the king's military officers in 2 Kgs. 25:19. This text does not specify exactly what kind of overseer.

▣ "second in command of the city" This may imply that he was next to Nehemiah's brother, Hanani (cf. Neh. 7:2). It is possible that Judah was the overseer of Benjamin's labor force who helped rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

The NIV translates this phrase "was over the Second District of the city." The only other English translation that I have found that has this interpretation is James Moffatt, A New Translation of the Bible. It is also in the footnote of the NEB.

11:11
NASB, NKJV   "the leader of the house of God"
NRSV   "officer of the house of God"
TEV   "who was High Priest"
NJB   "the chief of the Temple of God"

The term (BDB 617) means "one in front." It is used of political leaders, but also of religious leaders (cf. 2 Chr. 31:12; 35:8; Jer. 20:1, also of High Priest, 1 Chr. 9:11; 2 Chr. 31:13 [different word in Neh. 11:10]; Neh. 11:11; Dan. 11:22).

11:14
NASB, NRSV   "valiant warriors"
NKJV   "mighty men of valor"
TEV   "outstanding soldiers"
NJB   "outstanding people"
NET   "capable men"
REB   "men of substance"

This term (BDB 298) can refer to

  1. physical strength
  2. military prowess (e.g., Jos. 1:14; 8:3; 10:7; Jdg. 6:12; 11:1; 2 Chr. 13:3; 14:8)
  3. ability (cf. Neh. 11:6; Exod. 18:21,25; 1 Chr. 9:13)
  4. wealth (1 Sam. 9:1; 2 Kgs. 15:20)

Because these men are priests either #1 or #3 fits the context best.

NASB, NRSV   "the son of Haggedolim"
NKJV   "the son of one of the great men"
TEV   "a member of a leading family"
NJB   "men of substance"

The term (BDB 153, KB 177) means "great" and is used to describe many things and persons (NASB 1970 marginal note, p. 700, "the great ones"). The TEV translation carries the basic thought of the PLURAL form in this context.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:16 "who were in charge of the outside work of the house of God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:16 "who were in charge of the outside work of the house of God" In the context of Nehemiah, one wonders if this refers to

  1. normal temple activities, but done outside the precincts of the temple (e.g., raising sacrificial sheep)
  2. the work done on the walls and gates of the city which were near the temple area
  3. other administrative assignments (cf. 1 Chr. 26:29)

The term has the connotation in this text of secular work.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:17 "Asaph. . .Jeduthun"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:17 "Asaph. . .Jeduthun" These were two of the three groups of temple singers appointed by David (cf. 1 Chr. 25:1-4; 2 Chr. 5:12).

NASB   "who was the leader in beginning the thanksgiving at prayer"
NKJV   "who was the leader who began the thanksgiving with prayer"
NRSV   "who was the leader to begin the thanksgiving with prayer"
TEV   "He led the Temple choir in singing the prayer of thanksgiving"
NJB   "who led the praises and intoned the thanksgiving associated with the prayer"

This Levite was somehow related to the liturgical aspect of prayer/praise. The Hebrew "the begin" is close to the Hebrew "the praise" (cf. LXX & Vulgate). The JPSOA combines the meaning by "he would lead off with praise" (The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1706). The UBS Text Project, p. 540, gives "of the praise" a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

Asaph was a leader of a Levitical family involved in temple music and praise (cf. 1 Chr. 25:1-2; 2 Chr. 5:12).

▣ "and Bakbukiah, the second among his brethren" This seems to imply that this Levite was the assistant to Mattaniah (cf. TEV). This Hebrew term (BDB 1041) is often used to denote the second in charge/control/leadership (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:4; 25:18; 1 Chr. 5:12; 15:18; 2 Chr. 31:12; Jer. 52:24).

▣ "Abda the son of Shammua" 1 Chronicles 9:16 has Obadiah son of Shemaiah.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:18 Many of the Levites lived outside of the city of Jerusalem (cf. Neh. 11:3,20), but 284 did live in the city.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:19 "the gatekeepers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:19 "the gatekeepers" These were also ancient families who were appointed to this special task at the temple (cf. 1 Chr. 9:17-27; 23:5; Ezra 2:42).

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:20 "each on his own inheritance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:20 "each on his own inheritance" Originally the tribe of Levi did not inherit land. The Lord Himself was their inheritance (cf. Num. 18:20,24; Deut. 10:9; 18:1-2; Jos. 13:14,33). The Levites asked Joshua for houses in certain special cities called "Levitical cities" (cf. Joshua 21) along with a small part of the surrounding pasture land. In this way they could grow vegetable gardens or raise an animal.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:21 "the temple servants"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:21 "the temple servants" See note at Ezra 2:43.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:22 There are so many lists of people in Ezra and Nehemiah. Often the names are common. The only way to try to tell them apart is to

  1. check which group they are a part of (e.g., lay persons, priests, Levites, etc.)
  2. check the tribe
  3. check the order of the names

Here in Neh. 11:22 it is obvious that Uzzi is from the same family of Asaph mentioned in Neh. 11:17.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:23 "the king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:23 "the king" This refers to David, not Artaxerxes I (cf. Neh. 12:24,45-46). These temple personnel were appointed special tasks to perform in the temple on a regular basis, many of the tasks going back to David's day.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:24 "Pethahiah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:24 "Pethahiah" This is the name of a priest in David's day who was involved in the twenty-four divisions (cf. 1 Chr. 24:16).

There is another man by this same name mentioned in Neh. 11:24. The interpretive question is (1) do Neh. 11:23 and 24 go together and, thereby "the king" refers to David or (2) is the man a representative of Artaxerxes I, the Persian king during Ezra's and Nehemiah's day?

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:25 "Kiriath-arba"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:25 "Kiriath-arba" This is the ancient name for Hebron (cf. Gen. 23:2), which is 20 miles south of Jerusalem (cf. Jos. 14:15; 15:54; 20:7; Jdg. 1:10).

▣ "and its towns" This is literally the Hebrew idiom "daughters."

▣ "Dibon" This is possibly the same as Dimonah. See Jos. 15:21-26.

▣ "Jekabzeel" A village in southern Judah close to Edom. See Joshua 15:21.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:25, 28, 32, 34 "Jekabzeel. . .Meconah. . .Ananiah. . .Neballat"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:25, 28, 32, 34 "Jekabzeel. . .Meconah. . .Ananiah. . .Neballat" These are cities which appear only here in the Bible.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:25-36
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:25-36 The list of cities in chapter 3 which relates those who worked on the city wall is different from this list. The only name that is the same is Zanoah. This is hard to explain for the lists are supposed to be a list of the surrounding cities with Jewish populations. The possibilities are (1) that these cities mark the extent of the boundaries of Judah and Benjamin, not the cities close to Jerusalem or (2) that these are cities in the pre-exilic land allocations of Judah (cf. Neh. 11:25-30) and Benjamin (cf. Neh. 11:31-36) in which the returnees settled.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:26 "Moladah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:26 "Moladah" See Jos. 15:26; 19:2; 1 Chr. 4:28.

▣ "Beth-pelet" This is a village in southern Judah. See Jos. 15:27.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:27 "Hazar-Shual, in Beersheba"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:27 "Hazar-Shual, in Beersheba" Both are mentioned in Jos. 15:28.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:29 "En-rimmon"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:29 "En-rimmon" See Joshua 15:32.

▣ "Zorah" See Jos. 15:33.

▣ "Jarmuth" Like Lachish this was originally an Amorite city. See Jos. 10:3,5,23; 12:11; 15:35.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:30 "Zanoah, Adullam"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:30 "Zanoah, Adullam" Both are mentioned in Jos. 15:34-35.

▣ "Lachish" This was a major walled city (e.g., Jos. 10; 12:3-16; 2 Chr. 11:9; 22:9).

▣ "Azekah" This is a city of Judah located on the coastal plain. See Jos. 15:35.

▣ "Beersheba" This is about 32 miles south of Jerusalem. The current Persian land allocation for Judah did not extend that far north.

▣"the valley of Hinnom" One of the valleys in Jerusalem known as the location of the worship of the Phoenician fire god Molech. This valley was later used as the garbage dump for Jerusalem. Jesus uses it to describe Hell — Gehenna.

Special Topic: Where Are the Dead? II. D.

Special Topic: Molech

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:31 "Geba"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:31 "Geba" This was a northern city of Benjamin. Its name means "height" or "hill." See Joshua 18:24.

▣ "Michmash and Aija" Both are mentioned in Isa. 10:28-20. They were located near Bethel. Aija means "ruins" and may be a way of referring to Ai.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:32 "Anathoth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:32 "Anathoth" This was a Levitical city three miles north of Jerusalem (cf. Jos. 21:18). It was Jeremiah's hometown (cf. Jer. 1:1).

▣ "Nob" Another Levitical city two miles north of Jerusalem (cf. 1 Sam. 21:1; 22:9,11,19; Isa. 10:32).

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:33 "Hazor"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:33 "Hazor" Often these village names, like the people, are hard to identify because there are several by the same name. Hazor is a good example.

  1. a major Canaanite walled city in the north of Palestine (cf. Joshua 11; 12:19; 19:36)
  2. a small city in the south of Judah (cf. Jos. 15:23; 1 Kgs. 9:15)
  3. another city in southern Judah (Hazor-Hadattah, cf. Jos. 15:25)
  4. a small post-exilic city north of Jerusalem (cf. Neh. 11:33)
  5. this term even refers to countries or chiefdoms east of Arabia (cf. Jer. 49:28,30,33)

As an added point, people are hard to identify because

  1. in this period Levites and priests often used the names of ancestors
  2. in this period the Jewish families named their children after their grandfathers

▣ "Ramah" This is a city of Benjamin five miles north of Jerusalem. See Joshua 18:25; Judges 4:5; 19:13; Ezra 2:26.

▣ "Gittaim" The name means "two wine presses" and was northwest of Jerusalem. See 2 Sam. 4:3.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:34, 35 "Hadid. . .Lod and Ono"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:34, 35 "Hadid. . .Lod and Ono" See Ezra 2:33 and Neh. 7:37.

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:35 "the valley of craftsmen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:35 "the valley of craftsmen" The ancient guilds lived close together (cf. 1 Chr. 4:14).

entries.title: Nehemiah 11:36
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:36 As Neh. 11:25-30 describes the restored land of Judah in this Persian period, so Neh. 11:31-35 describes the extent of the land of Benjamin. The Levites lived in all areas of the restored land (cf. TEV).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:1 "Now these are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:1 "Now these are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel" The main return of exiled Israelites under Cyrus' decree occurred in 538 B.C. Documenting one's ancestry was very important for the returning exiles to verify their tribal lineage. This list is similar to, but has some differences in comparison with Ezra 2:36-39 and Neh. 7:39-47. The exact reasons for the differences are uncertain.

▣ "Ezra" This is not Ezra, the priest/scribe (cf. Ezra 7; 10; Neh. 8; 12:13,26,33,26).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

A. The purpose of the lists in this chapter (and for that matter the whole book) is difficult to grasp.

1. Neh. 12:1-11 refers to those who initially returned with Zerubbabel and Joshua.

2. Neh. 12:12-26 refers to a later group:

a. priests in Joiakim's (cf. Neh. 12:10) day

b. Levites in Eleashib's (cf. Neh. 12:10) day

3. Neh. 12:26 implies that the list in Neh. 12:22-26 were contemporaries with Ezra and Nehemiah.

4. Neh. 10:2-8 refers to Nehemiah's day (cf. Derek Kidner, Tyndale Commentary Series, p. 122).

 

B. In comparing all of these other lists in Ezra, Nehemiah, Chronicles, it seems that often priests identify themselves by a prominent ancestor instead of their personal name. The twenty-four divisions of King David (cf. 1 Chr. 23-24) become a guiding paradigm.

An additional problem is that the priestly families used the same names over and over again.

 

C. The problem of trying to put a date or historical setting to these names is clearly seen in that Mattaniah and Bakbakiah were Levitical leaders of antiphonal choirs in Zerubbabel's day (cf. Neh. 12:8-9) and Nehemiah's day (cf. Neh. 11:17).

 

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:4 "Ginnethoi"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:4 "Ginnethoi" The priest's name appears as Ginnethon in Neh. 10:6; 12:16 (and the Vulgate).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:8 "Mattaniah who was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:8 "Mattaniah who was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving" This was a common name among Levitical musicians. It is also mentioned in 1 Chr. 9:15; 2 Chr. 20:14; Neh. 11:17,22; 12:8,25,35.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:8-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:8-9 This list expands the list in Ezra 2:40-42 of Levites who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:9 "Unni"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:9 "Unni" The MT has (Kethiu‒written) Unno, but has a note that it should be read (Qere) as Unni.

▣ "stood opposite them in their service divisions" This may refer to liturgical or antiphonal singing aspects of worship (cf. 2 Chr. 7:6).

Because of Neh. 12:24 and the term "opposite" (BDB 617), which means "in front of," it may simply refer to the Levites being divided into twenty-four groupings to share the load of ministry (cf. 1 Chr. 23:6).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:10 "Jeshua. . .Joiakim. . .Eliashib"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:10 "Jeshua. . .Joiakim. . .Eliashib" Jeshua was the descendant of the last high priest when Jerusalem fell in 586 B.C. (cf. Ezra 3:2). Eliashib was the chief priest when Nehemiah arrived in Jerusalem in 445 B.C. (cf. Neh. 3:1).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:10-11 This is a 1ist of the High Priest's family, which may run into the Greek Period. Josephus (Antiq. 11.7.8) says Judda was high priest in 322 B.C.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:14 "Malluchi"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:14 "Malluchi" In Neh. 12:2 the name is spelled Malluch.

▣ "Shebaniah" Many assume he is the same as Shecaniah of Neh. 12:3.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:15 "Meraioth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:15 "Meraioth" Many assume he is the same as Meremoth of Neh. 12:3.

▣ "Helkai" Many assume he is the Hilkiah of Neh. 12:7.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:16 "Zechariah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:16 "Zechariah" This is the post-exilic prophet (519 B.C., cf. Zech. 1:1) linked with Haggai, Zerubbabel, and Joshua.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:20 "Sallai"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:20 "Sallai" Many assume he is the same as Sallu of Neh. 12:7.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:22 "Darius"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:22 "Darius" This either refers to the reign of Darius II (423-404 B.C., i.e., Josephus is inaccurate so Derek Kidner, Tyndale Commentary, pp. 143-146) or to the reign of Darius III (336-331 B.C., if Josephus' identifications are correct). Apparently, Jewish scribes had added to the genealogies unto their day.

Special Topic: Kings of Persia

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:23 "the book of the Chronicles"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:23 "the book of the Chronicles" This does not refer to the biblical book of I and 2 Chronicles, but to the temple records which Ezra and Nehemiah draw from freely.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:24 "the son of Kadmiel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:24 "the son of Kadmiel" The KJV has "Binnui." The UBS Text Project, p. 542, gives "son of" a "C" rating (considerable doubt), but suggests in its note that "son of" is probably the remains of the original reading, which was the name "Binnui."

▣ "as prescribed by David" See 1 Chronicles 23:6.

▣ "the man of God" This is a title used of Moses (cf. Deut. 33:1; Jos. 14:6). It was used of the prophets. In Hebrew theology one must be a prophet to write Scripture. Moses is called a prophet in Deuteronomy 18. David was considered to be the author of numerous Psalms; therefore, he too must be a prophet, a man of God (ish Elohim).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:25 "the storehouses of the gates"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:25 "the storehouses of the gates" There were storehouses in the temple in several locations.

  1. small rooms off of the central building
  2. small rooms at the gates

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:26 "in the days of Nehemiah. . .Ezra"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:26 "in the days of Nehemiah. . .Ezra" Those who assume that Ezra 7:7 is inaccurate and place Ezra after Nehemiah usually change or delete this verse and Neh. 12:36 and 38. This debate grows out of three theories concerning Ezra 7:7, "seventh year of King Artaxerxes."

  1. The traditional view has been to date this in 457 B.C. in the reign of Artaxerxes I.
  2. A second theory has been to suppose a scribal error, which should have been "twenty-seventh year of King Artaxerxes."
  3. The third theory supposes it to refer to Artaxerxes II which would be 398 B.C.

I like the first!

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:27 "cymbals, harps and lyres"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:27 "cymbals, harps and lyres" These were also used in Solomon's dedication of the temple (cf. 2 Chr. 5:13). These returnees tried to mimic Solomon's rituals, procedures, and actions.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:27-43
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:27-43 This section deals with the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem, which relates back to chapter 7. The FIRST PERSON SINGULAR PRONOUN "I" appears again (cf. Neh. 12:31), as it last did in Neh. 7:5.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:28 "Netophathites"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:28 "Netophathites" This was a city near Bethlehem (cf. Ezra 2:22; Neh. 2:26).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:29 "Beth-gilgal"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:29 "Beth-gilgal" Beth means "house" or "place." Gilgal means "wheel" or "circle." There are two possibilities:

  1. the first camp site of Joshua in the Promised Land (cf. Jos. 4,5,10), near Jericho
  2. a place twelve miles north of Shechem (cf. 2 Kgs. 2:1; 4:38) associated with Elijah and Elisha

▣ "Geba" This means "height" or "hill." It was a Levitical city of Benjamin (cf. Joshua 21:17; 1 Sam. 13:3; 2 Sam. 5:25; 1 Chr. 6:60; 8:6; 2 Chr. 16:6; Neh. 11:31; 12:29; Isa. 10:29; Zech. 14:10).

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:30 "purified"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:30 "purified" This VERB (BDB 372, KB 369, used twice, the first Hithpael IMPERFECT and the second Piel IMPERFECT) means "cleanse" or "purify." The Piel form denotes cleansing:

  1. the altar of incense, Lev. 16:19
  2. the temple, 2 Chr. 29:15,16,18; Neh. 13:6
  3. Judah and Jerusalem, 2 Chr. 34:3,5,8
  4. of Jerusalem, Neh. 12:30
  5. the priesthood, Neh. 13:30
  6. the altar Ezek. 43:26

Often the cleansing was by blood or water.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:31 "two great choirs"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:31 "two great choirs" These two processionals started on the top of the western wall about in the middle (south of the temple). This was exactly where Nehemiah had started his nighttime reconnoitering (cf. Neh. 2:13-16). Ezra led one group (Neh. 12:36) south, counter clockwise, while Nehemiah followed with the other one north, clockwise (cf. Neh. 12:38). They met on the eastern wall level with the temple (the Gate of the Guard, Neh. 12:39).

For specific locations see notes at Nehemiah 3.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:31-43
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:31-43 This is the official dedication of the walls. How soon it followed their construction is uncertain. It was a religious occasion much like Joshua's covenant renewal at Shechem. It is unusual to dedicate a wall in the OT, but in reality it offered protection for the holy city and its holy temple.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:35 "trimpets"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:35 "trimpets" See Special Topic: Horns Used by Israel.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:44 "tithes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:44 "tithes" See Special Topic: Tithing in the Mosaic Legislation

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:44-47
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:44-47 This seems to be a parenthesis giving further information and not part of Nehemiah's first person account.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:45 "in accordance with the command of David and of his son Solomon"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:45 "in accordance with the command of David and of his son Solomon" See 1 Chronicles 23-26 and 2 Chr. 8:14.

entries.title: Nehemiah 12:47
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:47 The order of tithes is seen in Num. 18:21-32 (cf. Neh.10:38).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought provoking, not definitive.

1. How are the lists here and 1 Chr. 9 related?

2. Why are the lists of the cities in Neh. 11:25-36 and 3:lff different?

3. How are the lists of Nehemiah 12 and 7 related?

4. Were Ezra and Nehemiah contemporaries?

5. How were the priests supported?

entries.title: Nehemiah 13:1 "they read aloud from the book of Moses"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:1 "they read aloud from the book of Moses" The VERB (BDB 894, KB 1128) is a Niphal PERFECT. Whether this is an informal reading like Neh. 8:1-8 or a specifically called for reading like Deut. 31:11 the Feast of Tabernacles, is uncertain (cf. Neh. 8:4; 9:3).

These two post-exilic books are characterized by a reverence and desire for the word of God. They hear it and they respond in repentance and faith. The trend is set! They are becoming people of the book! At this point the book was about a thousand years old (i.e., depending on the date of the Exodus), but it was still relevant and crucial for their relationship with YHWH. Cultures change but revelation does not!

Special Topic: Moses' Authorship of the Pentateuch

▣ "there was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God" This is a direct reference to Deut. 23:3-6, which shows that the Mosaic law was available and well known.

This sounds so racist to us, but two things must be noted.

  1. These people had to restore a pure people unaffected by Canaanite or pagan culture and myths.
  2. Ruth, David's ancestor, was from Moab and she is in the line of the Messiah, as is Rachel the Canaanite prostitute!

Special Topic: Racism

Special Topic: Forever ('olam)

▣ "the assembly of God" This is the only place in the OT where the word for assembly, Qahal (BDB 874), and the word Elohim (BDB 43) are placed together. This term Qahal is what the translators of the Septuagint replace with ecclesia, which is the early church's self-chosen title. This shows they were identifying themselves with the Old Testament people of God.

Special Topic: Church (ekklesia)
